candidates.title: Improving Fuzzy Robustness in LLM Safety with Automated Red Teaming
candidates.finding: OpenAI reports a controlled model-safety study using adaptive automated red-team search with repeated success criteria (worst@n) to build adversarial training examples, then testing robustness against held-out and adaptive multi-turn attackers. Reported improvement applies to language-model safety refusals and training, not real robots, physical safety stops, consent, human keep votes or long-duration field reliability.
candidates.hilo_adaptation: Propose a synthetic-only, non-ranking stress-test plan for *evaluation tools* that repeats independently sampled adversarial/ambiguous intervention and stop-right scenarios, reports both worst-case failure and legitimate-task false-refusal rates, and requires a human review of each claim. Do not perform unapproved real-robot adversarial trials, train on sealed holdouts, modify frozen WANTED scoring/cohorts, import OpenAI data, infer human votes/field hours or claim physical certification.
